quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and FY2025 results (CFO, non-GAAP): Q4 revenue $244 million, up 9.4%; full-year revenue $901.3 million, up 15.2%, which the CEO said beat a China WFE market third parties estimate as generally flat for 2025 despite very little contribution from new products. Total shipments were $228 million in Q4, down 13.5%, and $854 million for the year, down 12.2%, against a tough compare (2024 shipments rose 63%) and some new-product shipments pushed into 2026. Gross margin was 41.0% in Q4 and 44.5% for the year (vs 50.4% in 2024); Q4 operating margin was 12.1% (vs 23.6%) and full-year 15.9% (vs 25.6%).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $244 million (+9.4%); FY revenue $901.3 million (+15.2%); Q4 shipments $228 million (-13.5%); FY shipments $854 million (-12.2%); Q4 gross margin 41.0%; operating margin 12.1%

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 product mix: single-wafer cleaning, Tahoe and semi-critical cleaning revenue was $159.9 million, up 3%; ECP (front-end and packaging), furnace and other technologies $64.1 million, up 23.9% (full year up 32.1%); advanced packaging excluding ECP, services and spares $20.5 million, up 23.8% (full year up 45.3%). Cleaning represented 69% of 2025 revenue and ACM estimates its cleaning portfolio now addresses 95% of application and process steps, targeting 100% in 2026. ECP front-end tools were about 70% of the ECP mix for the year and back-end (ECP AP) about 30%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 cleaning $159.9 million (+3%); ECP/furnace/other $64.1 million (+23.9%); advanced packaging $20.5 million (+23.8%); cleaning coverage 95% of process steps

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 gross margin fell 8.8 percentage points year-over-year, slightly below the 42% to 48% long-term target: product mix and margin pressure concentrated in a few semi-critical products (competitive pricing pressure amid a flood of new local China equipment entrants, often 5 or more players per point product) contributed about 5 points, and higher inventory provisions about 4 points. Management called it temporary and expects gross margin at the lower end of the target range in the first half of 2026 with a second-half lift from higher-margin newer products. 2026 plan: R&D 16% to 18% of sales, sales and marketing 7% to 8%, G&A about 6%, effective tax rate 8% to 10%; the CFO said 2026 operating margin comes in at the mid-teen level, similar to 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 gross margin down 8.8 percentage points (about 5 points mix, about 4 points provisions); 2026 R&D 16% to 18% of sales; tax rate 8% to 10%

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook: reiterated the revenue range introduced in mid-January of $1.08 billion to $1.175 billion (25% growth at the midpoint), with 2026 shipment growth expected to exceed revenue growth, driven by a strong product cycle in SPM cleaning and furnace, with supercritical CO2 dry, Track, panel-level plating and PECVD contributing some in 2026 but more in 2027 and beyond. Linearity: first half about 42%, 43% of revenue, second half 57% to 58%, Q1 about 18% to 20% of the full year. 2026 capital expenditures planned at about $200 million (2025: $58 million) for Lingang (mini line and second production facility), Oregon and other items. Long-term revenue target of $4 billion reaffirmed.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $1.08 billion to $1.175 billion; first half about 42%, 43% of revenue; Q1 about 18% to 20%; 2026 capex about $200 million

quarterly_data.signal: Customer momentum outside mainland China announced with the results: ACM delivered multiple single-wafer cleaning tools to the Singapore facility of its Asia-based foundry customer, its first tool installation in Singapore (tools in installation, expected to qualify and go into production this year, with copper plating behind). It also received advanced-packaging orders from 3 global customers: multiple wafer-level advanced packaging systems from a leading global OSAT based in Singapore (delivery Q1 2026), a panel-level advanced packaging vacuum cleaning tool from a leading global semiconductor packaging manufacturer based outside mainland China (delivery Q1 2026), and multiple wafer-level packaging systems from a leading North America-based technology customer (delivery later in 2026). The CEO added ACM has customers in Korea and potentially Taiwan (customers not named).
quarterly_data.figure: orders from 3 global customers; first tool installation to Singapore

quarterly_data.signal: Panel-level packaging: in Q4 ACM delivered its first Ultra ECP ap-p horizontal panel-level electroplating tool to an industry-leading large panel fabrication customer, which preferred horizontal plating over competitors' vertical plating for film uniformity and less cross-contamination. The CEO said ACM is the first, and likely the only, supplier of horizontal copper plating for panels, that plating has become the bottleneck for panel production expansion, and that a key Taiwan player wants only horizontal plating. ACM is engaging customers on 515 x 510 and 310 x 310 panel sizes, is offering panel plating, vacuum cleaning and bevel tools (with coater, developer, wet etcher and cleaning to follow), and expects additional panel POs this year in Taiwan, Korea and Singapore.
quarterly_data.figure: panel sizes 515 x 510 and 310 x 310; first horizontal panel-level electroplating tool delivered in Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Cleaning new products: SPM represents 25%, 30% of the cleaning market; ACM's new SPM nozzle design achieved a 50 nanoparticle size count of under 20 (which management believes is best-in-class) without routine chamber DI water cleaning, and ACM received a strong repeat SPM order from a major customer for delivery to module fab in 2026. The supercritical CO2 dry tool cuts CO2 consumption by approximately 40% versus competitors; demo POs for evaluation tools came from 2 customers for delivery in mid-2026. Management puts the incremental mainland China opportunity for these next-generation cleaning products at nearly USD 1 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: SPM 25%, 30% of cleaning market; particle count of under 20; supercritical CO2 dry demo POs from 2 customers; China opportunity nearly USD 1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 3D NAND: ACM's proprietary N2 bubbling wet etch is positioned for 3D NAND silicon nitride etching, where larger bubble size and uniformity control become more critical at 300 layer and above; the CEO said it covers today's 300-layer demand and addresses uniformity issues as the industry moves to 400 or even 500 layer, with demand seen both in China and globally.
quarterly_data.figure: 300 layer and above; 400 or even 500 layer

quarterly_data.signal: China market share: the CEO estimated ACM's China cleaning share at about the 35% range, expanding to 50%, 60% over the next few years (long-term objective approximately 60%), and its China ECP share at more than 40%, with a goal of 60% or more; cleaning is expected to outgrow China WFE in 2026 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: China cleaning share about 35% range; China ECP share more than 40%; long-term goal 60%

quarterly_data.signal: New platforms and footprint: furnace revenue was relatively small in 2025 with a more meaningful contribution expected in 2026 after breakthroughs in LPCVD, ALD and PEALD (demand including the 1,350-degree high-temperature version). The 300 WPH KrF track tool delivered last September is expected to reach mass-production qualification in 2026; in Q4 ACM delivered its first Ultra Lith BK system, its entry into the display panel market. Its PECVD platform has 3 trucks per chamber and multiple evaluation tools are expected to ship near term. The Oregon facility is expected to begin operation in the second half of 2026 as an evaluation site and initial US production base, partly to reduce tariff exposure.
quarterly_data.figure: 300 WPH KrF track tool; 1,350-degree furnace; Oregon operation expected in the second half of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and supply: total inventory was $702.6 million at year-end versus $676.4 million at the end of Q3; raw materials rose to $349.7 million, up $23.5 million quarter-over-quarter, on additional strategic purchases to support production plans and mitigate potential supply chain risk. Net cash was $845.5 million versus $259.1 million, including $623 million net raised in ACM Shanghai's 2025 private offering; in February 2026 ACM sold approximately 4.8 million ACM Shanghai shares at RMB 160 per share for approximately $111 million gross proceeds, earmarked mainly for global sales and marketing.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory $702.6 million; raw materials $349.7 million (up $23.5 million); net cash $845.5 million; $111 million gross proceeds
